# HKS Misinformation Review

> A peer-reviewed academic journal from Harvard Kennedy School publishing rigorous research on misinformation, disinformation, and interventions like prebunking and fact-checking.

HKS Misinformation Review is an open-access, double-blind peer-reviewed journal focused on advancing the scientific understanding of misinformation and disinformation across elections, social media, generative AI, and cultural phenomena. The journal publishes research articles, research notes, commentaries, and editorials with a strong emphasis on methodological rigor and practical interventions.

## Getting Started

- [HKS Misinformation Review](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu): Homepage for Harvard Kennedy School's peer-reviewed journal on misinformation research
- [About Us](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/about-us): Mission, editorial team, and institutional affiliations of the journal
- [Metrics](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/our-metrics): Journal metrics including CiteScore 7.6, usage stats, and publication speed

## Featured Research

- [People rely on their existing political beliefs to identify election misinformation](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/people-rely-on-their-existing-political-beliefs-to-identify-election-misinformation): Digital diary study on how political beliefs influence misinformation detection by Park, Lee, and McGuinness
- [On the same page? Experts are mostly, but not always aligned about disinformation in times of generative AI](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/on-the-same-page-experts-are-mostly-but-not-always-aligned-about-disinformation-in-times-of-generative-ai): Expert survey on generative AI's role in disinformation by Weikmann et al.
- [Prebunking misinformation techniques in social media feeds: Results from an Instagram field study](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/prebunking-misinformation-techniques-in-social-media-feeds-results-from-an-instagram-field-study): Large-scale Instagram field experiment on prebunking emotionally manipulative content
- [Emotional resonance and participatory misinformation: Learning from a K-pop controversy](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/article/emotional-resonance-and-participatory-misinformation-learning-from-a-k-pop-controversy): Case study on emotional narratives and participatory misinformation in K-pop

## All Content Types

- [Research Article](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/explore/research-article): Published research articles on election misinformation and political beliefs
- [Research Note](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/explore/research-note): Research notes on generative AI and disinformation mitigation
- [Commentary](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/explore/commentary): Expert commentary on informational systemic risk and election disinformation
- [Editorial](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/explore/editorial): Editorial overview of Volume 5 2024 research on misinformation and conspiracy theories
- [Most Cited](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/most-cited): Archive of most-cited articles on misinformation, fact-checking, and prebunking interventions

## For Authors & Reviewers

- [Author Guidelines](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/submit): Manuscript submission guidelines and publication process for authors
- [Editorial Policies](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/editorial-policies): Double-blind peer review policies and editorial decision criteria
- [Publication Ethics](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/our-publication-ethics): COPE-aligned publication ethics, authorship guidelines, and AI disclosure requirements
- [Become a Reviewer](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/review): Peer reviewer recruitment with Ph.D. candidate requirements and $100 stipend

- [Open Access and Licensing](https://misinforeview.hks.harvard.edu/open-access-and-licensing): Creative Commons CC-BY open access and licensing information
